name: Dysostosis of Genetic Origin

criteria.description: Presence of congenital malformations of bones including abnormal ossification and segmentation defects
Identification of pathogenic variant in genes known to cause dysostosis
Characteristic radiographic findings such as absent or malformed bones and abnormal bone shape
Positive family history of similar skeletal abnormalities
Presence of limb asymmetry, digital anomalies, or craniofacial dysmorphisms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital bone malformations with characteristic radiological abnormalities plus genetic confirmation of pathogenic variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on genetic testing and radiological evaluation due to phenotypic heterogeneity.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biochemical markers identified
imaging: Radiographs showing absent or hypoplastic bones, abnormal vertebral segmentation, and delayed ossification centers
CT and MRI may reveal detailed bone malformations and spinal anomalies
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes involved in bone development and ossification (e.g., HOX genes, TBX genes, or others depending on subtype)
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance patterns
Prenatal ultrasound may detect skeletal abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic skeletal involvement with metabolic abnormalities
Distinct genetic mutations different from dysostosis genes
Predominant craniofacial involvement with characteristic facial features

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress due to thoracic cage malformations
Progressive neurological deficits from spinal cord compression
Rapidly worsening limb deformities impairing function
